prompt: AppService currently only has createUser, with no way to list users back. Add an in-memory users array to AppService populated by createUser, a GET /users endpoint (AppController.listUsers), and a new ListUsersDto validated by class-validator (@IsOptional/@IsInt/@Min/@Max) for optional page and limit query params (limit capped at 100), returning a paginated slice via the app's existing global ValidationPipe. Put ListUsersDto either in src/create-user.dto.ts or a new src/list-users.dto.ts.
rationale: New resource + idiomatic Nest DTO validation, exercising the already-configured ValidationPipe.

checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const paths=['src/create-user.dto.ts','src/list-users.dto.ts']; const hit=paths.map(p=>fs.existsSync(p)?fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8'):'').join('\n'); if(!/ListUsersDto/.test(hit)||!/@IsOptional/.test(hit)||!/limit/.test(hit)||!/page/.test(hit)) process.exit(1); const svc=fs.readFileSync('src/app.service.ts','utf8'); if(!/listUsers/.test(svc)) process.exit(1);"

prompt: AppService.createUser returns a raw string like 'Creating user with name: X and email: Y', forcing API consumers to parse prose instead of reading structured data. Refactor createUser (and AppController's POST /users handler) to return { message: string; user: { name: string; email: string } } instead.
rationale: API-design code smell: a string response replaced with a proper structured JSON contract.
